title: Longitudinal Measurement of Extracellular Matrix Rigidity in 3D Tumor Models Using Particle-tracking Microrheology
protocol: Mix 10 ml of cell culture grade water with 0.1 g of agarose to obtain a 1% agarose solution.
Heat the agarose solution above 70 °C.
Aliquot 40 μl of agarose solution into each well on a 96-well plate.
Incubate the plate at 37 °C for at least 1 hour.
Harvest cells using standard techniques.
Determine the concentration of cells in the suspension with a hemacytometer.
Dilute cell suspension to 1,000 cells/ml.
Add 100 μl of diluted cell suspension to each well containing the cured agarose bed.
Place the sample on a shaker overnight at 37 °C and 5% CO2.
Incubate spheroids until desired diameter is reached.
Remove sample from shaker.
Add 100 µl of cell culture media.
Prepare a work station with needed materials inside a laminar flow hood.
Mix 2 parts stock carboxylate-modified 1 μm diameter fluorescent tracer probes to 25 parts sterile water.
Aliquot 125 μl of bovine collagen into an empty 2 ml vial.
Add 50 μl of diluted tracer probe solution to the vial containing the collagen.
Vortex briefly to distribute probes.
Add 235 μl of appropriate cell culture media containing phenol red for a total volume of 410 μl.
Vortex briefly before removing 205 μl and placing it in a new 2 ml vial.
Add ~2 μl of 1 M NaOH to Vial 1 to bring the solution back to neutral pH.
Vortex briefly to mix, then return Vial 1 to ice rack immediately.
Check the well containing the tumor spheroid after media removal.
If the spheroid was removed, add the 40 μl containing the spheroid to Vial 1.
If not, place the 40 μl back into the well and repeat the previous step.
Gently stir Vial 1 before transferring the mixture in 60 μl portions into three separate wells of a 96-well plate.
Inspect each well with a microscope after adding mixture to determine which well contains the spheroid.
Add ~2 μl 1 M NaOH and 40 μl of cell culture media to Vial 2 and vortex before aliquotting 60 μl of this mixture to an empty well in the 96-well plate and labeling as a control.
Place the plate in a 37 °C incubator to cure for at least 1 hr.
Transfer the sample plate from the incubator to the microscope stage.
Allow 10 min for the sample to equilibrate with the room temperature if a heated stage is not available.
Observe the sample with low powered objective lenses to make sure it is intact and ready for imaging.
Determine the tumor position within the well.
Decide how many sample points to take.
Move the stage to each desired position.
Use microscope interfacing software to record the x and y coordinates at each point.
Switch the microscope to a high powered objective lens (typically 100X).
Select the appropriate filter cube for the excitation wavelength of the tracer probes.
Move to the first point in the grid using the list of points created previously.
Adjust the focus to find the bottom of the well.
Move up to find a field of view containing several in-focus tracer probes.
Observe the intensity histogram and adjust the exposure intensity and time to give the greatest dynamic range possible while ensuring that the image does not become saturated.
Obtain a video sequence at a frame rate of 20-30 msec per frame (approximately 800 frames or 16-24 sec in length).
Save the video sequence with an appropriate convention.
Do not touch the microscope or table during recording.
Repeat steps for each sample point in the grid.
Repeat all steps from selecting points to saving videos for each well in the experiment.
Copy all video data to an analysis folder (possibly on a different computer).
Import image data into MATLAB or other analysis software.
Calibrate the software by analyzing several frames of the video to appropriately determine selection and rejection parameters for identifying probe center positions.
Automatically determine each probe position for all video frames using the calibrated software.
Link these positions into trajectories.
Compute the mean squared displacement (MSD) as a function of lag time, applying the appropriate spatial calibration factor.
Calculate G* using the generalized Stokes-Einstein relation considering the limits of applicability for the sample.
Repeat steps 4.2 through 4.6 for each field of view in the experiment.
Co-register position data from step 3.4 with viscoelastic modulii at a particular frequency of interest.
Use a custom routine or tabulate position data manually based on microscope metadata.
Generate a spatial rheology map of the ECM using 3D interpolation functions.
